title: Optimize Conductor 2.0 - Release Notes and Migration Guide
author: Ava Nguyen
body:
Summary

This document describes the Redwood Optimize Conductor 2.0 release: what changed, why it matters, SLO and billing impacts, rollout and migration steps, and operational notes for customers and internal teams. Optimize Conductor 2.0 introduces workload-aware multi-pass optimization, a pluggable estimator for hybrid deployments, and default telemetry schemas for per-route cost attribution. The release is focused on reducing per-token inference cost for conversational workloads while preserving quality SLAs.

Highlights

- Workload-aware multi-pass optimization: a new orchestration layer that simulates alternate batching, quantization, and cache policies across historical traces and recommends per-route profiles.
- Hybrid estimator plugin: customers running Dedicated + Private topologies can use the new estimator to predict cross-environment cost tradeoffs and warm-capacity benefits.
- Observability schema v2: standardized telemetry fields for capture of per-variant latency, KV cache hit rates, and token-level cost estimates (see Telemetry changes section).
- Migration assistant CLI: a guided CLI and UI assistant that validates a tenant’s usage traces, runs a sandboxed simulation, and produces recommended policy bundles with confidence bands.
- Compatibility and fallbacks: automatic fallback rules to Produce Conductor 1.x profiles when runtime compatibility or regression risks are detected.

Why this release?

Customers have asked for more deterministic cost reductions without manual tuning. Optimize Conductor 2.0 is intended to:

- reduce average per-token serving cost for chat-like flows by 8–22% in early benchmarks,
- shorten time-to-safe-rollout (canary → A/B → 100%) via integrated simulation-driven confidence scores, and
- provide clearer observability to map cost changes to specific configuration deltas.

What’s changed (detailed)

1) Multi-pass optimization engine
- Runs a sequence of optimizers (batch sizing, prefix caching, quantization profile selection, KV eviction policy) against a tenant’s trace in a sandbox.
- Produces an ordered set of recommended policy bundles with: expected cost delta, expected latency delta (p50/p95), and a confidence score derived from simulation variance.
- Output format (JSON example):

  {
    "bundle_id": "optc-202612-sandbox-01",
    "candidate_policies": ["batch-128","q8_2","prefix-kv-enabled"],
    "estimated_cost_change_pct": "-12.4",
    "estimated_latency_p95_ms": "210",
    "confidence": "0.87"
  }

2) Hybrid estimator plugin
- Extensible plugin API that accepts per-region capacity profiles and returns cross-topology allocations.
- Useful for customers who split traffic between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
- Sample CLI call: redwood-optimize simulate --tenant TENANT_ID --plugin hybrid-estimator --trace traces/2026-11-01.json

3) Observability schema v2
- New required telemetry fields: optimize.bundle_id, optimize.simulation_confidence, optimize.estimated_cost_usd, optimize.kv_hit_rate, optimize.batch_shape.
- Backwards compatibility: the ingestion pipeline will accept v1 telemetry but only the new dashboards and reports will show v2 fields.

4) Migration assistant CLI/UI
- Provides an automated sequence: validate traces → run sandbox sim → produce recommended bundles → run offline regression evals → generate rollout plan.
- CLI example (high level):

  # validate traces and run simulation\  redwood-optimize migrate validate --tenant TENANT_ID --trace s3://bucket/trace-2026-10-15.json\  redwood-optimize migrate simulate --tenant TENANT_ID --policy-bounds "{\"min_batch\":32,\"max_batch\":256}"

- The UI exposes an interactive confidence slider for selecting more conservative vs aggressive bundles.

SLO and billing impacts

- Expected unit economics: Early benchmarks across 6 representative tenants show mean cost reduction 12% (range 8–22%) with p95 latency change within +/- 10% of baseline for the chosen conservative bundles.
- Billing: There is no immediate change to billing metrics or pricing SKUs. Cost savings are realized through optimization of runtime configuration and will show up as lower consumption in token/cpu/GPU usage reports.
- SLA considerations: Teams must validate per-tenant latency/p95 and function-call integrity. Optimize Conductor 2.0 includes a safety gate that will not permit an automatic rollout if p95 regression > 15% in the sandbox regression evals.

Upgrade and migration plan (for customers)

Recommended staged migration (small-to-large tenants):

1) Prepare (owner: customer success / solutions engineering)
- Gather a 7–14 day usage trace covering representative traffic (session length distribution, model variants, peak windows).\- Ensure trace contains at least 50k inference requests or the migration assistant will flag low-confidence recommendations.
- Confirm tenant has a staging route (non-production) that can proxy 5–10% of live traffic for A/B tests.

2) Simulate and validate (owner: customer success + tenant engineering)
- Run the migration assistant simulate command to generate candidate bundles.
- Review recommended bundles and associated confidence scores.
- Run offline regression evals against a fixed prompt set to verify functional parity (owner provides known-good prompts for critical flows).

3) Canary rollout (owner: tenant engineering + Redwood SRE)
- Apply conservative bundle to 1–2 production routes at 1–5% traffic.
- Monitor optimize.simulation_confidence, optimize.estimated_cost_usd, request.latency_p95, model.output_consistency metrics for 24–72 hours.
- If p95 regression remains < 10% and no functional regressions detected, proceed to A/B.

4) A/B and ramp (owner: customer success + Redwood product)
- Ramp to 25–50% traffic, compare endpoint KPIs, and collect user-facing error rates.
- Typical ramp cadence: double traffic every 12 hours if all checks pass.

5) Full rollout and post-rollout audit (owner: customer success + finance)
- Ramp to 100% when confidence remains high.
- Generate a 7-day post-rollout audit report showing realized cost delta and latency impact.

Rollback criteria

Immediate rollback triggers:
- p95 latency regression > 15% vs baseline for the route during the canary or A/B.
- Any functional regression detected by the offline regression evals (semantic inconsistency, hallucination increase measured by test oracle).
- KV/cache hit rate drop > 30% causing unexpected cost increases.

Operational runbook (SRE)

Owner: eng-sre

Monitoring checklist (alerts to configure):
- optimize.simulation_confidence < 0.5 for a recently applied bundle → alert to product/sre.
- optimize.estimated_cost_usd increases > 10% over rolling 24h → alert to billing-ops.
- request.latency_p95 increases > 12% over baseline → page oncall.
- optimize.kv_hit_rate falls below configured threshold for a route → run cache debug runbook.

Quick debug steps:
1) Identify affected routes using optimize.bundle_id in logs.
2) Use the simulation sandbox to replay a representative subset of traffic.
3) If rollback is required: redwood-optimize migrate rollback --tenant TENANT_ID --bundle BUNDLE_ID
4) Open an incident and follow standard oncall postmortem cadence if the cause is not apparent.

Compatibility and fallbacks

- Compatibility matrix: Conductor 2.0 supports runtime agent versions >= 3.2.2. If a route uses agent < 3.2.2, the migration assistant will recommend a v1-compatible bundle and include an upgrade path.
- Fallback behavior: If a live trial detects functional regressions, the platform will automatically apply the last-known-good bundle for that route and create a high-visibility ticket to the product owner.

Telemetry and dashboard changes (what product teams should know)

- New Optimize dashboards (Console):
  - Per-tenant Optimization Summary (shows realized vs estimated cost deltas, per-route confidence scores).
  - Bundle Explorer (lists applied bundles, simulation metadata, and rollback events).
  - Regression surface map (maps prompts/paths that failed offline regressions).

- Telemetry ingestion notes: SDKs and ingestion pipelines must emit the optimize.* v2 fields. Agents older than 3.2.2 will continue to emit v1 fields; the ingestion layer will backfill where possible but v2-only reports require agent upgrade.

Administrative and billing notes

- There is no separate paid SKU for Optimize Conductor 2.0 during the initial preview period. Usage of the migration assistant sandbox is metered and shown as an internal optimization run in the tenant’s console.
- Finance ops will track realized savings as part of monthly consumption reports. For enterprise customers on committed Dedicated plans, Optimize-driven savings will be reconciled as operational improvements and reflected in future commit discussions.

Known limitations and gotchas

- Small tenants (fewer than 50k requests in the trace window) should expect lower-confidence recommendations; consider a longer trace window.
- Extremely bursty traffic patterns can reduce optimizer confidence; the migration assistant offers a conservative bundle option for these tenants.
- The sandbox simulation assumes identical model weights and versioning; if a tenant uses rapidly changing model variants, freeze model rollouts during sandbox runs.

Appendices

A — Example recommended bundle (full JSON)
{
  "bundle_id": "optc-202612-conservative-001",
  "policies": {
    "batch": 64,
    "quantization": "q8_2",
    "prefix_kv_enabled": true,
    "kv_eviction_policy": "lru_time_based_1h"
  },
  "estimated_cost_change_pct": "-9.8",
  "estimated_latency_p95_ms": "195",
  "confidence": "0.78"
}

B — CLI checklist for migration assistants
- Ensure trace is complete and covers peak windows.
- Run redwood-optimize migrate validate --tenant TENANT_ID --trace s3://...
- If validation passes, run redwood-optimize migrate simulate --tenant TENANT_ID --plugin hybrid-estimator
- Review candidate bundles and run offline regression evals
- Execute canary rollback plan if any regression triggers occur

C — Release timeline
- 2026-11-15: internal alpha completed
- 2026-11-22: customer preview starts (select tenants)
- 2026-12-01: general availability (GA) and documentation published

D — Links (internal)
- Migration assistant repo: github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/migration-assistant
- Telemetry schema v2 reference: /product-docs/design-specs/optimize-telemetry-schema-v2
